analysis: Reviewed the head-side excerpts of landing/package-lock.json (lines 2368-3920). The change is a lockfile-only dependency refresh: next 16.2.6 to 16.4.1, sharp and its @img/* optional packages 0.34.5 to 0.35.5, libvips 1.2.4 to 1.3.4, and a nested postcss 8.5.23. Other packages in the visible range include eslint 9.39.3, jsdom 29.1.1, js-yaml 4.3.2, lru-cache 11.5.3, fast-uri 3.1.9, flatted 3.4.4, picomatch 2.3.2 and 4.0.7, and tldts 7.4.18. All visible resolved URLs point to registry.npmjs.org and all entries carry sha512 integrity hashes. I saw no git, tarball-URL or non-registry sources and no missing integrity fields. No install scripts or hasInstallScript flags appear in the visible hunks. The landing site is a Next.js marketing app (darkbloom-landing). It is outside the provider and native-runtime scope of this threat model, and it does not touch the coordinator-provider WebSocket, attestation, key custody, App Attest authorization, prefix cache or the add-on hold socket (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, TB-012). I identified no impact on assets A-001 to A-018. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated, and the head ranges I could not see (lines 1-2367 and 3921 onward, including the @img/sharp-* integrity entries at roughly 626-1060 and 1599-1662) were not reviewed. I did not verify the integrity hashes against the registry. The new 'next' version 16.4.1 and sharp 0.35.5 are taken from the lockfile as given. I did not check whether package.json matches the lockfile, since it is not in the supplied units. No security regression is evident in the supplied lines.
